title: Modernize remote build cache and slim polyglot toolchain
creator: Riley Chen
description: We are seeing large variability in CI build latency and frequent cache misses across languages (Node, Go, Python). Our current Docker base images are large and inconsistent, CI uses a mixed set of local caches and ad-hoc s3 artifacts which causes flaky cache hits and long developer feedback loops. This ticket will consolidate on a BuildKit-based remote cache (CAS/registry-backed), introduce smaller purpose-built base images for runtime and tooling ("primer" images), and centralize toolchain installation to stable builder images to reduce cache churn and per-job bootstrap time.
background: Historically we relied on per-repo Dockerfiles and per-job install steps (nvm/pyenv/go install) which increase layer variability. Previous attempts (ENG-33921, ENG-41399) reduced some churn but did not standardize a remote cache. Benchmarks show median build time for a typical PR has stagnated at ~9m with tail (95th) > 28m and cache hit rate ~45% for large TS/Go services.
proposal: 1) Enable BuildKit remote cache using an internal CAS backed by object storage + registry layers. 2) Create slim 'primer' base images per language/runtime that contain pinned toolchains (node 20.x, go 1.21, python 3.11) and common OS packages. 3) Replace ad-hoc install steps in CI with --mount=type=cache and --cache-from/--cache-to BuildKit flags. 4) Split lint/test into separate pipelines that reuse the same cached layers to avoid re-installing toolchains. 5) Add a periodic cache-priming job that warms popular monorepo paths. 6) Add telemetry (cache hit rate, restored bytes, build time) to the CI dashboard.
tasks: Create BuildKit remote cache PoC (agent + CAS config) and document cost model
Design 'primer' base images: node-primer:20, go-primer:1.21, py-primer:3.11 and publish to internal registry
Refactor representative service Dockerfiles (api-service, infra-cli, frontend) to use buildkit mounts and primer images
Add CI steps to push and pull cache layers using --cache-to=type=registry,ref=... and --cache-from=...
Implement cache-priming cron job for top 20 paths identified in build telemetry
Update lint/test pipelines to consume cached toolchains and validate no functional regressions
Add observability: CI exporter for cache hit/miss, median build time, 95th percentile, layer size distribution
Write migration guide for internal teams and run 2-week pilot with infra and frontend squads
Create rollback plan and feature flag toggle in CI to disable remote cache if it regresses builds
acceptance_criteria: End-to-end proof of concept with at least 3 services showing >60% cache hit rate
Median CI build time for a representative PR decreases by >=35% compared to baseline
95th percentile CI build time decreases by >=25% and tail failures due to network cache access <1%
Primer images are published and consumed by >=5 active repos during pilot
Observability dashboard shows cache hit/miss, restored bytes, and build time with alerts for regression
Migration guide reviewed and approved by developer experience and security teams
rollout_plan: Week 0: PoC and cost estimate; create primer images and basic BuildKit agent
Week 1: Integrate with 2 low-risk repositories (infra-cli, internal-tools) and measure cache behavior
Week 2: Expand to frontend and api-service; run cache-priming job daily; validate metrics
Week 3: Collect feedback, fix regressions, update docs; opt-in for other teams via self-serve guide
Week 4: Flip default CI to use remote cache for monorepo jobs; monitor for 2 weeks then mark Done
risks_and_mitigations: Risk: Remote cache availability or permission issues cause CI failures. Mitigation: fallback to local cache and add fast failover toggle in CI config.
Risk: Increased storage costs for remote CAS. Mitigation: tiered retention policy, TTL for unused cache entries, and cost telemetry to monitor spend.
Risk: Primer images include vulnerable packages. Mitigation: Bake images in a hardened pipeline with image scanning and SBOM; schedule monthly base updates.

Risk: Build semantics differ slightly (BuildKit vs docker builder) causing subtle behavior changes. Mitigation: run canonical end-to-end smoke tests and include a short validation step when enabling cache per repo.
notes: We chose registry-backed cache over pure CAS for operational simplicity and portability across cloud regions.
Primer images will be minimal (avoid heavy dev tools) and an opt-in 'dev-full' variant will include IDE helpers for internal CI jobs only.
This project should reduce token and runtime costs by lowering repetitive bootstrap work across jobs and improving developer iteration speed.
Related: coordinate with Platform team for IAM roles and with Security for image signing and KMS access.

qa_steps: Run full CI for api-service and frontend with remote cache enabled and compare logs to baseline
Verify that lint/test pipelines use cached toolchains by inspecting step durations
Force a cache miss and ensure fallback to local build completes within SLA
Run security image scan on primer images and verify SBOM is present
final_decision: Proceed with BuildKit remote cache and primer images. Pilot successful for initial repos; follow-up tickets created for large-layer fallback (ENG-431508) and monthly image rotation. Next: expand pilot and finalize migration guide.
